_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Morocco covering Berber heritage, Phoenician/Roman Mauretania, Arab conquest, Idrisid dynasty, Almoravid/Almohad empires, Marinid/Saadian/Alaouite dynasties, French/Spanish protectorates, independence under Mohammed V, Hassan II's Years of Lead, and Western Sahara claim.

ethnic_groups.name: Arab/Arabised Berber
ethnic_groups.notes: Majority Arab or Arabised; Arabic-speaking; historically Berber populations Arabised post-7th century; ethnic boundaries fluid

ethnic_groups.name: Berber (Amazigh)
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous North Africans; three major groups: Riffians (North, Rif Mountains, Tarifit language), Berbers of Middle Atlas and Eastern High Atlas (Tamazight), Shilha/Tashelhit-speakers (Souss Valley, Anti-Atlas, Western High Atlas); Berber majority in rural mountain areas

ethnic_groups.name: Haratin
ethnic_groups.notes: Black Moroccans; Saharan oases; Draa and Tafilalt; historically marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Gnawa
ethnic_groups.notes: Descendants of sub-Saharan slaves; distinct musical and spiritual tradition

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Sahrawi, European, Jewish)
ethnic_groups.notes: Sahrawi Arabs (Western Sahara); small French community; historically significant Jewish community (mostly emigrated post-1948)

country_profile.notes_unique: Home to the University of al-Qarawiyyin (859 CE), recognised as the world's oldest existing university; controls most of disputed Western Sahara; the only African country bordering the Mediterranean and Atlantic.

natural_resources.notes: World's largest phosphate reserves (~75% of global reserves) controlled by OCP Group; fisheries (Atlantic sardines); growing renewable energy sector (Noor-Ouarzazate solar complex, one of world's largest CSP plants); cannabis (recently legalised for medical/industrial use); automobile manufacturing hub (Renault, Stellantis).

military.notes: Royal Armed Forces (FAR); sixth-largest military in Africa; extensive US military cooperation; involved in Western Sahara (UN MINURSO ceasefire observers); 2020 US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara; modern equipment (F-16s, M1 Abrams pending); compulsory military service reintroduced 2019.

infrastructure.notes: Al Boraq HSR; 1800km motorway network; Tanger Med mega-port; IAM, Orange, Inwi telecoms.

debt_aid.notes: Middle-income economy; Maroc 2030 Vision; Tanger Med port (largest in Africa/Mediterranean); high-speed rail (Al Boraq, Africa's first TGV); Mohammed VI investment fund; earthquake reconstruction ($11.7B programme).

education.notes: Al-Qarawiyyin is recognised as world's oldest existing university; bilingual (Arabic/French) education with growing English; PISA performance below average; Francophone business schools; large student population; rural-urban education gap.

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 5 million+ (France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Netherlands, Germany, Israel, Canada)
diaspora_migration.notes: Remittances critical (~7.5% GDP); large diaspora in Europe; becoming transit/destination country for sub-Saharan migrants; regularisation programmes for African migrants; Moroccan Jews in Israel (~700,000 of Moroccan descent).
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: Transit country for sub-Saharan migrants to Europe; regularization campaigns (2014, 2017)

digital_economy.notes: Africa's largest tech park (Casablanca Technopark); auto-industry digitalisation; Maroc Telecom, Orange, inwi operators; submarine cables; nearshoring destination for European companies; Huawei cloud data centre.

geography.terrain: Atlas Mountains (High, Middle, Anti-Atlas); Rif Mountains in north; Atlantic/Mediterranean coasts; Sahara in southeast; fertile plains (Chaouia, Doukala, Gharb)
geography.notes: Gateway between Europe and Africa; 14 km from Spain (Strait of Gibraltar); Atlas Mountains; only African country with Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts; Saharan south.

economy_extended.notes: 6th largest African economy; OCP Group (#1 phosphate exporter globally); automotive (Renault, Stellantis—2nd exporter in Africa); aerospace cluster; Tanger Med port (#1 in Africa/Mediterranean); 2030 FIFA World Cup co-host.

health.notes: AMO mandatory health insurance expanding; COVID-19 vaccination success (one of Africa's highest rates); 2023 earthquake (Al Haouz) disaster response; healthcare reform underway.

food_agriculture.notes: Plan Maroc Vert (Green Morocco Plan, 2008); argan oil (UNESCO Biosphere); phosphate fertilizer exporter (OCP); drought vulnerable; cannabis legalized for medical/industrial use (2021).

energy.notes: Noor-Ouarzazate solar complex (world's largest CSP); Tarfaya wind farm; target 52% renewables by 2030; Morocco-UK power cable planned; ONEE utility.

transport.notes: Al Boraq high-speed rail (1st in Africa, Tangier–Casablanca, 320 km/h); extensive highway network; Tanger Med mega-port; 2030 World Cup infrastructure investments.

tourism.notes: #1 tourist destination in Africa; 9 UNESCO sites; Marrakesh iconic; desert tourism; cultural richness; 2030 FIFA World Cup (with Spain, Portugal).

human_rights_gender.notes: 2004 Moudawana (family code) reform (women's rights milestone); press freedom concerns; Western Sahara human rights scrutiny; low women's economic participation.

security_stability.notes: Strong security apparatus (DGSN, DGST, Gendarmerie); effective counter-terrorism; September 2023 Al Haouz earthquake (3,000+ deaths); Algeria border closed since 1994.

national_symbols: pentacle (Star of David on flag—actually Seal of Solomon)
cultural_heritage.film_industry: Growing (Ouarzazate 'Africa's Hollywood'; Atlas Studios; international film location)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: 2M, Al Aoula (state); Medi1 TV; Le360, Hespress (online); Al Jazeera popular; some press restrictions
cultural_heritage.notes: Amazigh+Arab+Andalusian+Jewish+Saharan cultural mosaic; monarchy (Alaouite dynasty since 1631); world's oldest university (al-Qarawiyyin, 859 CE); zellige tilework; literary tradition.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Civil law (French system) with Islamic law elements
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Personal status (Moudawana family code); Islam state religion
legal_system.customary_law_role: Amazigh customary law in some rural areas
legal_system.notes: Constitutional monarchy; King holds significant executive/religious authority (Amir al-Mu'minin); 2011 constitutional reform post-Arab Spring; Supreme Council of Judicial Power.

comparative_rankings.notes: Major African economic and diplomatic power.

current_leader.title: King
current_leader.notes: Alaouite dynasty; son of Hassan II; Commander of the Faithful; political and religious authority; modest reforms; Western Sahara claim

former_monarchs.name: Sultan Mohammed V
former_monarchs.notes: Led independence movement; resisted Vichy deportation of Jews; exiled by France 1953–1955; father of the nation

former_monarchs.name: King Hassan II
former_monarchs.notes: 38-year reign; survived coup attempts 1971/1972; Years of Lead (Les Années de Plomb) repression; Green March 1975 (Western Sahara); late reforms
